title.narrative: MN - Development of the national urban housing strategy in Mauritania

description.narrative:
The population of the Islamic Republic of Mauritania is estimated at 4,462,000 in 2019, based on a growth rate of 2.17% (2017), a life expectancy of 63 years, a literacy rate of 52.1% and an age distribution shown in Table 1. Nomads have decreased from 12% in 1988 to 1.9% in the 2013 Census (approximately 66,328 people). The employed population makes up 40.6% of the working age population, and 55.4% of this number resides in urban areas, where it is mainly employed in administration (30%) and commerce (33%), which has a high level of informality. Most of these people live in precarious neighborhoods, many of which are currently being rehabilitated. In addition, the government is promoting a policy of regrouping nomads on the basis of national standards.
In order to meet the current challenges and future requirements of urban populations, the government plans to implement a national urban housing strategy. This strategy would be inspired by the guidelines of the Sustainable Development Goals and the principles of the New Urban Agenda. The general approach made up of three (3) major steps, coherent as follows:
Step 1: Rapid participatory assessment of the situation of the urban housing (Systems and Trends in housing development - Priority problems, strengths and weaknesses of the Priority problems, strengths and weaknesses of the system)
Step 2: Analysis and evaluation of needs (Definition of orientations - orientations and conditions favorable to the provision of decent housing and urban services for the greatest number of people
Step 3: Elaboration of a national urban housing strategy (Action plan; Definition of the institutional, legal and regulatory framework).
These will be preceded by the establishment of coordination mechanism to facilitate data collection, review and validation of reports.
The main expected outcomes are:
Outcome 1: Strengthened coordination mechanisms for the elaboration and validation of the participatory diagnosis of urban housing challenges and perspectives
Outcome 2: Increased tools for the enhancement of the co-production of safer, resilient, inclusive and sustainable urban housing
